reasoning: Yoaz Hendel's Reservists party, later reported as running together with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party, polled around 3 to 5 seats through 2025-26. That is roughly at or slightly above the 3.25% threshold. Under 2.75% corresponds to fewer than about 3.3 seats' worth of votes. Small centre-right protest parties polling near the threshold are often squeezed on election day by strategic voting, as Jewish Home was in 2022. That makes a sub-2.75% result plausible. On the other hand, a merger or joint run with a larger opposition list (e.g., Bennett or Eisenkot) would push the counted share far above 2.75%. Polling above the threshold also suggests a solo run would more likely land around 3-4%. A withdrawal scenario adds ambiguity. Weighing these, I estimate roughly a one-in-three chance.
